subject: A dedicated TD build adds adjustable terminal image glow and is ready for Parker to test.
reader: Parker liked cool-retro-term, asked for a dedicated branch and a slider, and returns from being away to test the native build.

sections.heading: Image Glow
sections.text:
You liked the light spilling off the letters in cool-retro-term. That effect now has its own TD branch and a native slider. A separate test window is waiting on workspace 4 , with a glowing pane beside a reference pinned at zero. 

GAUGES → CRT → image glow 

01 · NATIVE OUTPUT 

 0% · reference capture 
 55% · native capture 

 Recorded strength: 0% 55% 100% 

 Figure 1. Light spreads around the letters while their sharp core remains visible. These are crops of real GPU captures at matching coordinates, not a browser recreation. Buttons select recorded states. Source: the isolated release build on this machine’s RTX 3080 Laptop GPU.

sections.heading: The dial
sections.text:
Open the bottom bar’s GAUGES button, expand CRT, and turn image glow . The outer control affects panes that follow it. Each pane can own a different strength through its existing GAUGES control; the right-hand reference already owns zero. 

02 · THE NATIVE CONTROL 

The slider runs from 0% to 100%. CRT must be on; warp can stay at zero. 
 Close GAUGES to see the result. The existing tray suppresses the CRT pass while open. This preview limitation remains tracked in the glass-preview issue . 
CRT off keeps the chosen strength, so switching it back on restores the glow. Strength and per-pane ownership survive a restart. 
 Figure 2. Image glow sits beside the other CRT dials. Source: a second isolated native fixture. This screenshot shows zero glow and does not claim a live preview while dragging.

sections.heading: The light
sections.text:
The renderer reads bright neighbours from its existing scene texture and blends their light into each terminal’s image. Every sample is checked against that pane’s bounds. The effect uses sixteen neighbour samples per affected pixel and adds no history texture. 

03 · RENDERING BOUNDARY 
 Figure 3. A pane can glow without lighting its neighbour. The drawing follows the new shader. It describes the mechanism; GPU frame cost has not been benchmarked.

sections.heading: The checks
sections.text:
The native fixture held its text still while the outer strength changed. Comparisons cover the left and right terminal grids, excluding window chrome: 900 × 1,020 and 860 × 1,020 physical pixels respectively. 
 | 
 | Check | Observed result 

 | 100% glow | 75,184 changed pixels in the glowing grid; zero in the reference. 

 | Return to zero | Both grids match their zero-glow captures exactly. 

 | CRT off, strength retained at 100% | Both grids match zero glow exactly. 

 | Restart from saved settings | 55% follows outer; the reference stays pinned at 0%. No replacement seed was written. 

 | Default terminal core | 2,594 passed; 10 ignored 

 | Fallback Alacritty core | 2,541 passed; 10 ignored 

 | Build and lint | Locked release build, format check, both core Clippy gates and patch replay passed. 

Evidence: native configuration and restart receipt · pixel comparison · test commands and counts . Passing checks cover this machine and these fixtures. Multi-monitor frame cost and other GPUs remain unmeasured.

sections.heading: Your test window
sections.text:
The session is named phosphor-glow-test . Left starts at 55%; right is pinned at 0%. Both panes are ordinary interactive Bash shells. The binary and its settings live in a private lab directory; the normal TD installation and session 1 remain in place. 

sh /home/parker/Work/td-phosphor-glow-lab/native-lab/launch.sh 

 Glow strength 
Try your usual dense terminal output at 25%, 55% and 100%. Mark the strength you want as the starting point, or leave a note on a capture where the halo makes a letter harder to read. 

Branch: feat/crt-phosphor-glow · base: main · release: unassigned. 
Inspiration: cool-retro-term . Its effect code is GPL-3.0-or-later; this shader was independently implemented. This build provides image bloom. Fading phosphor history remains a separate possible effect.
